text_blocks.snippet: For 2025, single-employer plans will see a flat-rate per-participant premium of $106, up from $101 in 2024. The variable-rate premium remains at $52 per $1,000 of unfunded vested benefits, with a per-participant cap of $717, up from $686 in 2024. Multiemployer plans will pay a flat-rate premium of $39 per participant, increased from $37 in 2024.

list.snippet: Single-Employer Plans:
Flat-rate premium: $106 per participant.
Variable-rate premium: $52 per $1,000 of unfunded vested benefits.
Variable-rate premium per participant cap: $717.
Multiemployer Plans:
Flat-rate premium: $39 per participant.

text_blocks.snippet: Additionally, the premium filing and payment due date for 2025 plan years is accelerated by one month. For calendar-year plans, this means premiums are due on September 15 instead of October 15.

text_blocks.snippet: The Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC) uses various interest rates for different purposes related to pension plans. These rates are used to determine the value of pension benefits, premiums, and other financial aspects of pension plans. For example, the PBGC uses interest rates to calculate the value of lump-sum payments for certain terminated pension plans. Additionally, the PBGC uses interest rates to determine the variable-rate premiums that some employers pay to the agency. The PBGC also utilizes interest rates in its regulations for allocating assets in single-employer plans.
Here's a breakdown of the different types of PBGC interest rates and their uses:

list.snippet: The PBGC uses a specific interest rate to determine the variable-rate premium that some employers pay based on their plan's unfunded vested benefits.
This rate is tied to the yield on 30-year Treasury securities and is published monthly.
For premium payment years beginning in 2025, the variable-rate premium remains at $52 per $1,000 of unfunded vested benefits.
The flat-rate premium for single-employer plans for 2025 is $106 per participant, up from $101 in 2024.
For valuation dates on or after July 31, 2024, the PBGC uses a yield curve tied to market conditions for the ERISA 4044 interest assumption.
This yield curve is defined as of the last day of the month and is used for valuation dates on or before that date.
The PBGC provides the 4044 yield curves in a spreadsheet format to simplify calculations.
The PBGC also uses interest rates to determine the value of benefits when a plan terminates and the PBGC becomes trustee.
The PBGC's interest rate assumptions are also used in the allocation of assets in single-employer plans.
The IRS also publishes interest rates that are relevant to PBGC calculations, particularly for late or defaulted withdrawal liability.
These rates are used to calculate interest on unpaid contributions as of the termination date.
The PBGC website (pbgc.gov) is the primary source for information on PBGC interest rates.
The PBGC's website provides historical data on applicable Federal mid-term rates.
The IRS website (irs.gov) provides information on minimum present value segment rates.
The PBGC's website (pbgc.gov) provides information on variable-rate premiums and their associated interest rates.
